ranking: Live ranking of free, open-source FM-1 firmware, rebuilt on every update check from the cicloid/awesome-fm-1 list (Custom firmware → Open source) and a GitHub repository search, scored ln(1+stars) + ln(1+total .fwsc downloads). Top 10 get cards, #11–#30 the list. Only projects with a GitHub release carrying a .fwsc image count. Free closed-source firmware (FM-1+VA, April OS) has no stars or download counts to compare, so it gets its own curated, unranked section. Paid firmware (Groove OS) is left out. Projects without a curated entry get a card from their GitHub metadata, marked "not curated yet". Offline fallback: firmware/directory.json.

firmware.name: Stock V15
firmware.author: M-VAVE
firmware.summary: The firmware the FM-1 ships with: Dexed/msfa-derived 6-operator FM, 32 algorithms, 12 voices, arpeggiator, step sequencer and multi-FX. The only firmware the dashboard's Voice and FX editors target. Community firmwares expect you to be on V15 first.
firmware.install: Flash with M-UPGRADE (Windows, in this library after download): extract the zip, run it, load FM-1.fwsc. Most community installers also offer "Return to official V15".

traits.sourceNote: M-VAVE's factory firmware; no source published.
traits.revertNote: This is stock. M-UPGRADE (Windows) reinstalls it, and most community installers can too.

firmware.name: FM-1 Open
firmware.author: M-VAVE
firmware.summary: M-VAVE's official open firmware (October 2026): 6-op FM, 303-style bass, 808-style drums, chiptune, pluck and a sampler on independent tracks. App source is GPLv3 with an SDK linking exception; the sound engine ships as a binary SDK. Free.
firmware.install: Flash and edit from the browser workbench (Chrome/Edge over USB). The release also carries an offline copy of the workbench (HTML) and the development kit.

traits.sourceNote: App source GPLv3 (SDK linking exception); the sound engine is a binary SDK.
traits.revertNote: The workbench's "flash back to stock V15" (刷回原厂 V15) reinstalls V15 and its 128 factory voices.

firmware.name: Felucca
firmware.author: hugelton
firmware.tagline: Multi-engine synth the others build on
firmware.summary: Multi-engine synth by Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton Instruments): FM, VA, phase distortion, chiptune, sampler, granular, physical modelling, organ and drums; four tracks, 64-step sequencer with conditional steps and Euclid, song mode, MIDI learn, USB audio. The platform most other firmwares are forked from. GPL-3.0.
firmware.install: Web installer (Chrome/Edge, USB) or tools/fm1_install.py. The installer can return to official V15.

traits.revertNote: The installer's "Return to official V15" puts stock back (it asks for your unmodified FM-1.fwsc).

firmware.name: SLOOP
firmware.author: 3dSam (isod89)
firmware.summary: Live groovebox: three synth layers plus a drum machine, 37 drum kits, punch-in effects, layer system, song mode and a standalone HTML editor. Based on Felucca. GPL-3.0.
firmware.install: Web installer (Chrome/Edge, USB). USB rescue: hold OCT− while switching on.

traits.revertNote: The installer's "Install the official V15" puts stock back (it asks for your FM-1.fwsc).

firmware.name: X0X
firmware.author: Charles Vestal
firmware.summary: TR-909, TR-808, two TB-303s with TB-3PO acid generators and a breakbeat slicer, each with its own sequencer. Felucca fork. GPL-3.0.

traits.revertNote: The installer's "Back to the stock firmware" puts stock back.

firmware.name: Melodee
firmware.author: keremimo
firmware.summary: Felucca derivative that went its own way: ten engines (incl. SID), eight patterns per track, STUDIO workspaces, four-channel USB audio input, TR-808 kit. Interrupted writes return to USB update mode. Ships a standalone fm1-recover tool. GPL-3.0.
firmware.install: Web installer (Chrome/Edge, USB). Black screen: use fm1-recover (Windows zip in this library) or M-UPGRADE.

traits.revertNote: The installer's "Return to official V15" puts stock back (it asks for your unmodified FM-1.fwsc). Black screen: fm1-recover from the release.

firmware.name: ChoralRoot
firmware.author: Quixotic7
firmware.summary: One hand plays roots, the other shapes chords, with voicings, key modes, bass and a looper. Built on Felucca. GPL-3.0. A single-core build is also published.

traits.revertNote: The installer's "Return to official V15" puts stock back (it asks for your unmodified FM-1.fwsc).

firmware.name: FoMni
firmware.author: Charles Vestal
firmware.summary: Strum the white keys, pick chords on the black ones, with rhythm patterns and auto bass. GPL-3.0.

traits.revertNote: The installer's "Back to the stock firmware" puts stock back.

firmware.name: GHOULBOX
firmware.author: Jason Persinger
firmware.summary: Cathedral reverb, worn-tape effect, hurdy-gurdy engine with drones, dark ambient presets and an old-RPG screen. 53-page PDF guide. USB rescue if it fails to start twice. Felucca fork. GPL-3.0.
firmware.install: Web installer (Chrome/Edge, USB data cable, no other music app open).

traits.revertNote: The installer's "Return to official V15" puts stock back (it asks for your unmodified FM-1.fwsc).

firmware.name: AMB-1
firmware.author: Charles Vestal
firmware.summary: Generative ambient machine inspired by Music for Airports that plays itself from power-on: tape loops of unequal length, gliding bass, Euclidean percussion. GPL-3.0.

traits.revertNote: The installer's "Back to the stock firmware" puts stock back. Validation: the first try left a black screen, the second worked.

firmware.name: Jangada
firmware.author: zednaked
firmware.summary: Felucca fork adding superwave analog, a modulation matrix, latched drones, ratchets and synthesized drum kits, with a web editor and studio. GPL-3.0.
firmware.install: Web installer on the project site (Chrome/Edge, USB).

traits.revertNote: The installer's "Back up and install the official V15" puts stock back.

firmware.name: Skiff
firmware.author: illuminus5
firmware.summary: Six tracks, fourteen synth and drum engines, 143 factory sounds, a 64-step sequencer with chords, ratchets, trig conditions and parameter locks, patterns, songs and a browser editor. Built on Felucca. GPL-3.0.

traits.revertNote: The installer's "Return to official V15" puts stock back (it asks for your unmodified FM-1.fwsc).

firmware.name: FM-1+VA
firmware.author: Baud Girl
firmware.tagline: The first custom firmware: VA engine + 64-step sequencer
firmware.summary: The first third-party FM-1 firmware, by Madeline (Baud Girl). Keeps the stock FM engine and adds a virtual analog engine (BLEP oscillators, supersaw, several filters), an 8-bit engine with drums and arpeggios, a 64-step dot-matrix sequencer with ratchets and chance, pattern chaining and song mode, four assignable knobs on every screen, two-button navigation and colour themes. Free; closed source (the author has said the source will be released).
firmware.install: Web installer on baudgirl.com (Chrome/Edge on a computer, Chrome on Android). Presets and patterns are kept. No return-to-stock in its installer: use M-UPGRADE with the library's FM-1.fwsc (needs FM-1+VA 94 or later; with 93 or earlier M-UPGRADE fails with "Checksum error"), or another project's "Return to official V15".

traits.sourceNote: Free, closed source; the author has said the source will be released.
traits.revertNote: No return-to-stock in its installer: M-UPGRADE with FM-1.fwsc (FM-1+VA 94 or later), or another installer's "Return to official V15".

firmware.name: April OS
firmware.author: beashoko
firmware.tagline: SK-1-style sampler: record with your phone or laptop mic
firmware.summary: Sampling firmware in the spirit of the Casio SK-1: no synth engines, only samples. 32 sample slots of three seconds, an eight-track sequencer, a sample and loop editor, and recording through a computer's or iPhone's microphone via the installer page. A Felucca fork; its repository holds the installer page, not the firmware source. Free.
firmware.install: Web installer page (Chrome/Edge, USB); the firmware is built into the page, so there is no separate .fwsc to download. No return-to-stock button found: use M-UPGRADE with the library's FM-1.fwsc, or another project's "Return to official V15".

traits.sourceNote: Free; a Felucca fork whose repository holds only the installer page, not the firmware source.
traits.revertNote: No return-to-stock button in its installer: M-UPGRADE with FM-1.fwsc, or another installer's "Return to official V15".

policy: Free firmware only: paid packages are never listed.
